concepts.name: SimpleGraph
concepts.statement: Type u → Type u
concepts.formal_statement: Type u → Type u
concepts.description: A simple graph is an irreflexive symmetric relation Adj on a vertex type V.

source.docstring:
A simple graph is an irreflexive symmetric relation `Adj` on a vertex type `V`.
The relation describes which pairs of vertices are adjacent.
There is exactly one edge for every pair of adjacent vertices;
see `SimpleGraph.edgeSet` for the corresponding edge set.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.name: SimpleGraph.Walk
concepts.statement: {V : Type u} → SimpleGraph V → V → V → Type u
concepts.formal_statement: {V : Type u} → SimpleGraph V → V → V → Type u
concepts.description: A walk is a sequence of adjacent vertices.

source.docstring:
A walk is a sequence of adjacent vertices.  For vertices `u v : V`,
the type `walk u v` consists of all walks starting at `u` and ending at `v`.

We say that a walk *visits* the vertices it contains.  The set of vertices a
walk visits is `SimpleGraph.Walk.support`.

See `SimpleGraph.Walk.nil'` and `SimpleGraph.Walk.cons'` for patterns that
can be useful in definitions since they make the vertices explicit.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.name: SimpleGraph.Subgraph
concepts.statement: {V : Type u} → SimpleGraph V → Type u
concepts.formal_statement: {V : Type u} → SimpleGraph V → Type u
concepts.description: A subgraph of a SimpleGraph is a subset of vertices along with a restriction of the adjacency relation that is symmetric and is supported by the vertex subset.

source.docstring:
A subgraph of a `SimpleGraph` is a subset of vertices along with a restriction of the adjacency
relation that is symmetric and is supported by the vertex subset.  They also form a bounded lattice.

Thinking of `V → V → Prop` as `Set (V × V)`, a set of darts (i.e., half-edges), then
`Subgraph.adj_sub` is that the darts of a subgraph are a subset of the darts of `G`.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.statement: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → Prop
concepts.formal_statement: {V : Type u_1} → SimpleGraph V → Prop
concepts.description: A graph G consists of a set of cycles, if each vertex is either isolated or connected to exactly two vertices.

source.docstring:
A graph `G` consists of a set of cycles, if each vertex is either isolated or connected to
exactly two vertices. This is used to create new matchings by taking the `symmDiff` with cycles.
The definition of `symmDiff` that makes sense is the one for `SimpleGraph`. The `symmDiff`
for `SimpleGraph.Subgraph` deriving from the lattice structure also affects the vertices included,
which we do not want in this case. This is why this property is defined for `SimpleGraph`, rather
than `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`.

concepts.name: Finpartition.equitabilise
concepts.statement:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : DecidableEq α] →
    {s : Finset α} →
      {m a b : ℕ} → {P : Finpartition s} → a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card → Finpartition s
concepts.formal_statement:
{α : Type u_1} →
  [inst : DecidableEq α] →
    {s : Finset α} →
      {m a b : ℕ} → {P : Finpartition s} → a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card → Finpartition s
concepts.description: Given a partition P of s, as well as a proof that a * m + b * (m + 1) = #s, build a new partition Q of s where each part has size m or m + 1, every part of P is the union of parts of Q plus at most m extra elements, there are b parts of size m + 1 and (provided m > 0, because a partition does not have parts of size 0) there are a parts of size m and hence a + b parts in total.

source.docstring:
Given a partition `P` of `s`, as well as a proof that `a * m + b * (m + 1) = #s`, build a
new partition `Q` of `s` where each part has size `m` or `m + 1`, every part of `P` is the union of
parts of `Q` plus at most `m` extra elements, there are `b` parts of size `m + 1` and (provided
`m > 0`, because a partition does not have parts of size `0`) there are `a` parts of size `m` and
hence `a + b` parts in total.
source.note: Exact exported declaration. Import is NOT a local compiler or axiom audit.

concepts.description: A graph G is alternating with respect to some other graph G', if exactly every other edge in G is in G'.

source.docstring:
A graph `G` is alternating with respect to some other graph `G'`, if exactly every other edge in
`G` is in `G'`. Note that the degree of each vertex needs to be at most 2 for this to be
possible. This property is used to create new matchings using `symmDiff`.
The definition of `symmDiff` that makes sense is the one for `SimpleGraph`. The `symmDiff`
for `SimpleGraph.Subgraph` deriving from the lattice structure also affects the vertices included,
which we do not want in this case. This is why this property, just like `IsCycles`, is defined
for `SimpleGraph` rather than `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`.

concepts.name: Finpartition.equitabilise_aux
concepts.statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} {m a b : ℕ} {P : Finpartition s},
  a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card →
    ∃ Q,
      (∀ x ∈ Q.parts, x.card = m ∨ x.card = m + 1) ∧
        (∀ x ∈ P.parts, (x \ {y ∈ Q.parts | y ⊆ x}.biUnion id).card ≤ m) ∧
          {i ∈ Q.parts | i.card = m + 1}.card = b
concepts.formal_statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} {m a b : ℕ} {P : Finpartition s},
  a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card →
    ∃ Q,
      (∀ x ∈ Q.parts, x.card = m ∨ x.card = m + 1) ∧
        (∀ x ∈ P.parts, (x \ {y ∈ Q.parts | y ⊆ x}.biUnion id).card ≤ m) ∧
          {i ∈ Q.parts | i.card = m + 1}.card = b
concepts.description: Given a partition P of s, as well as a proof that a * m + b * (m + 1) = #s, we can find a new partition Q of s where each part has size m or m + 1, every part of P is the union of parts of Q plus at most m extra elements, there are b parts of size m + 1 and (provided m > 0, because a partition does not have parts of size 0) there are a parts of size m and hence a + b parts in total.

union of parts of `Q` plus at most `m` extra elements, there are `b` parts of size `m + 1` and
(provided `m > 0`, because a partition does not have parts of size `0`) there are `a` parts of size

  [inst_2 : DecidableEq V] {v w : V},
  G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ →
    v ≠ w → ¬G.Adj v w → (G.neighborFinset v ∪ G.neighborFinset w).card = 2 * k - μ
concepts.formal_statement:
∀ {V : Type u} [inst : Fintype V] {G : SimpleGraph V} [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj] {n k ℓ μ : ℕ}
  [inst_2 : DecidableEq V] {v w : V},
  G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ →
    v ≠ w → ¬G.Adj v w → (G.neighborFinset v ∪ G.neighborFinset w).card = 2 * k - μ
concepts.description: Assuming G is strongly regular, 2*(k + 1) - m in G is the number of vertices that are adjacent to either v or w when ¬G.Adj v w.

source.docstring:
Assuming `G` is strongly regular, `2*(k + 1) - m` in `G` is the number of vertices that are
adjacent to either `v` or `w` when `¬G.Adj v w`. So it's the cardinality of
`G.neighborSet v ∪ G.neighborSet w`.
